headline: Billions spent, yet Saudi Arabia struggles to stop Houthi attacks
summary: Despite massive defense spending, Saudi Arabia is finding it difficult to protect key assets from Houthi missiles and drones.
details: Saudi Arabia, a powerful Middle Eastern nation, spends hundreds of billions of dollars annually on its defense sector.
However, the kingdom is struggling to protect critical infrastructure, including airports, oil refineries, and pipelines, from attacks by the Houthi armed group from Yemen.
The Houthis have developed a strategy of coordinating long-range drones with ballistic and cruise missiles to overwhelm Saudi defense systems.
This tactical approach is noted to be similar to the strategies employed by Russia in recent conflicts.
The continued vulnerability of key assets despite high spending highlights a significant gap in the defense capabilities of the kingdom.
caption:
Billions of dollars in defense spending, but key assets are still vulnerable. Why is Saudi Arabia struggling to stop Houthi attacks?

Saudi Arabia, a powerful Middle Eastern nation, spends hundreds of billions of dollars annually on its defense sector.

However, the kingdom is struggling to protect critical infrastructure, including airports, oil refineries, and pipelines, from attacks by the Houthi armed group from Yemen.

The Houthis have developed a strategy of coordinating long-range drones with ballistic and cruise missiles to overwhelm Saudi defense systems.

This tactical approach is noted to be similar to the strategies employed by Russia in recent conflicts.

The continued vulnerability of key assets despite high spending highlights a significant gap in the defense capabilities of the kingdom.

headline_marked: 4 lakh students [[drop out of secondary education]] in one year
headline: 4 lakh students drop out of secondary education in one year
summary: New data reveals a sharp decline in secondary school enrollment, while Madrasas and English medium schools see an increase.
details: According to the Bangladesh Education Statistics-2025 report by BANBEIS, over 400,000 students have left secondary education within a single year.
The decline is evident in general secondary schools, as well as independent technical and vocational institutions, where enrollment has dropped to 650,000.
In contrast, Madrasas have seen an increase of over 43,000 students, and English medium schools have added 595 students in the past year.
While the number of secondary schools increased by 94, the total student population in these institutions fell from 7.8 million to 7.4 million.
Experts suggest the decline may be caused by learning gaps following the pandemic, child labor, early marriage, and financial crises facing families.
A previous study by the Dhaka Education Board found that 41% of absent SSC candidates—mostly girls—had married, highlighting a systemic issue.
Education experts, including Professor S.M. Hafizur Rahman, emphasize the need for deep research to understand the trends and take necessary corrective actions.
caption:
Over 400,000 students left secondary education in just one year. Why is this happening?

According to the Bangladesh Education Statistics-2025 report by BANBEIS, over 400,000 students have left secondary education within a single year.

The decline is evident in general secondary schools, as well as independent technical and vocational institutions, where enrollment has dropped to 650,000.

In contrast, Madrasas have seen an increase of over 43,000 students, and English medium schools have added 595 students in the past year.

While the number of secondary schools increased by 94, the total student population in these institutions fell from 7.8 million to 7.4 million.

Experts suggest the decline may be caused by learning gaps following the pandemic, child labor, early marriage, and financial crises facing families.

A previous study by the Dhaka Education Board found that 41% of absent SSC candidates—mostly girls—had married, highlighting a systemic issue.

Education experts, including Professor S.M. Hafizur Rahman, emphasize the need for deep research to understand the trends and take necessary corrective actions.
